thread:
maria: Hey all — hitting a weird one in the Java SSE client. When the server finishes a streaming response the final JSON array chunk sometimes arrives split so the parser never gets the closing bracket. Repro in our integration tests. Anyone seen an EOS/boundary vs backpressure interplay here?
chen: Yup saw something similar last week. Is your client using Netty ByteBuf -> InputStream bridge?
maria: Yep, Netty handler converts ByteBuf to a byte[] and calls listener.onData(bytes). Parser expects to get complete NDJSON objects but sometimes final ']' comes in a separate small chunk and our consumer decides it's done (reads -1) before parser sees it.
ashok: Could be due to aggressive windowing/autoRead off + small buffer flush. Are you using a bounded queue for the parser thread?
maria: We do — bounded ArrayBlockingQueue(256). Producer enqueues chunks, consumer dequeues and feeds Jackson JsonParser incremental API. If producer detects slow consumer we drop/merge or signal end-of-stream earlier. That might be the bug.
julie: Quick question: what does your EOF detection look like? InputStream.read returning -1 vs explicit server 'event: done' frame?
maria: We rely on read() == -1. But Netty sometimes signals channelInactive which we translate to enqueue(EOF_MARKER) — race with chunk arrival.
chen: Two angles: 1) handle split UTF-8 sequences across chunks; 2) treat EOF as "no more data" but only finalize parser once all queued chunks processed. If you finalize on EOF immediately you can lose trailing bytes.
maria: Good point. Currently the code does: if (b == EOF_MARKER) { parser.close(); } which closes without ensuring queue drained.
ashok: Proposed fix: when EOF_MARKER seen, set a flag and only close parser after consumer processed queue to empty. Also ensure producer enqueues any leftover byte[] before EOF.
julie: Another robustness: use parser.feedInput(byte[], offset, len) style and only call parser.endOfInput() after last feed. For Jackson incremental streaming: call JsonFactory.createNonBlockingByteArrayParser and then parser.endOfInput(); that signals finalization cleanly.
maria: Thanks. Two follow-ups: 1) how to avoid backpressure deadlocks if consumer is blocked waiting on parser while producer is stuck because queue full? 2) any tests we should add?
chen: For (1) don't block Netty IO thread — offload enqueue to worker thread. If you're blocking Netty because queue full, connection stalls and you might hit reconnects. Use Channel#config().setAutoRead(false) to apply backpressure to Netty and resume once queue has room.
ashok: For (2) add a test that sends final tiny chunk (single-byte ']') after a pause while reader thread is sleeping to simulate race. Also test multi-byte UTF-8 boundaries and a scenario where channelInactive arrives before final chunk is handed to queue.
maria: Implementing patch now. Quick sanity check on pseudo code, does this look sound?
```
producer: onByteBuf(buf) -> enqueue(copy(buf)); // never block IO thread
producer: onChannelInactive -> enqueue(EOF_MARKER)
consumer: while true {
  chunk = dequeue(timeout)
  if chunk == EOF_MARKER { eofSeen=true; if queueEmpty() { parser.endOfInput(); break } else continue }
  parser.feedInput(chunk,0,chunk.length)
}
if eofSeen && queueEmpty() parser.endOfInput()
```
chen: Looks reasonable. Minor: use a special wrapper object instead of magic marker to avoid colliding with real zero-length chunk. Also prefer synchronous drain after EOF to avoid spin loops.
julie: Also add metrics: count partial-json errors, queue drops, and time-between-final-chunk and EOF to catch regressions.
maria: Good, will add. One more: any concerns about memory if a client stalls and queue grows?
ashok: Bounded queue prevents unbounded memory. But combine with autoRead=false and resume when queue occupancy < threshold to keep memory steady. Also set reasonable timeouts and connection-level max-inflight bytes.
maria: Patch uploaded: https://git.internal/r/redwood/streaming-java/pull/842 — added tests + docs. PTAL @chen @julie.
chen: Reviewing now, small nit about closing parsers in finally block.
julie: Approved tests look solid, left one comment about using StandardCharsets.UTF_8 when converting for logging.
stream-bot: CI: streaming-java #842 — unit tests passed, integration failed on flaky-sse-e2e (investigating).
maria: Thanks — will re-run e2e with increased timeouts and rerun. If flaky persists, I'll instrument the Netty handler to log chunk boundaries and channelInactive ordering.
chen: Thanks for driving this. Post-fix we should add a short doc in devex about SSE EOF semantics and Netty autoRead interplay.
maria: Agreed — I'll draft a 1-pager and drop in #docs. :thumbsup:
